sentences.text: Tytthostonyx was a genus containing only one known species, Tytthostonyx glauconiticus, a prehistoric seabird.
Scientists placed this bird in its own unique family called Tytthostonychidae.
Its fossils were discovered at the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary, marking the moment the dinosaurs vanished.
This creature lived during a span of over ten million years, from 72.2 to 61.66 million years ago.
The genus was formally described by Olson and Parris in 1987.
It was apparently closely related to the ancestors of modern seabirds like Procellariiformes and/or Pelecaniformes.
The Hornerstown Formation, where Tytthostonyx fossils were found, is the subject of much debate.
